rulings.challenge_claim: No byte claim in the row is false and the seam stands, but three defects: the English gloss set beside the Jer.6.6 splice covers neither end of what was spliced, dropping the four-word formula that opens it and adding a mound clause the splice does not contain; the formula the warrant rests on is a subordinated shape opening on a causal connective, quoted but not engaged, against the bare verse-initial formula at Jer.6.9, and the two are separate objects book-wide (29 verses against 153); and the frame-owner change that actually makes Jer.6.6 an onset, the besiegers' cry giving way to divine speech, is left implicit when a formula warrant owes the mouth.
rulings.grounds: Re-derived from the source bytes. The row's splice is the first seven words of MT 6:6 and re-collates at byte tier (oshb:Jer.6.6). Limb one is upheld and is the load-bearing defect: the English set beside that splice covers neither end of it. The splice opens on כִּ֣י כֹ֤ה אָמַר֙ יְהוָ֣ה צְבָא֔וֹת (oshb:Jer.6.6, byte tier), five words the gloss renders not at all, while the gloss's tail, “and cast up a mound against Jerusalem” (web:Jer.6.6), answers וְשִׁפְכ֥וּ עַל יְרוּשָׁלִַ֖ם סֹלְלָ֑ה (oshb:Jer.6.6, byte tier), four words that stand later in the verse and are not inside the splice. Fidelity is not the problem - the English is verbatim against the staged receiving text and carries its ref in the same field - the problem is extent, in both directions, and the unglossed head is exactly the formula the warrant rests on. Limb two is REFUTED on the bytes: the connective-plus-formula shape is attested at 29 verses book-wide (sweep: 29 verses, MT keys) and stands verse-initial at 28 of them, the one non-initial site being MT 24:8, so at MT 6:6 it is the book's standard subordinated-onset shape and not a buried subordinate clause; and the 29-verse shape is a strict subset of the 153-verse formula census (sweep: 153 verses, MT keys), a shape within its superset rather than a separate object. MT 6:6 also carries the plain armies title, a member of the 50-verse formula-plus-title set (sweep: 50 verses, MT keys), so both recorded substrate-signal keys are byte-correct here; the bare verse-initial כֹּ֤ה אָמַר֙ יְהֹוָ֣ה צְבָא֔וֹת (oshb:Jer.6.9, byte tier) is a second onset three verses on, not a standard the seam fails. Limb three REFINES: the incoming mouth is in fact given - the splice carries the divine name and title and the prose calls the speech divine - so what is missing is the OUTGOING frame owner, the attacking force's own summons at ק֖וּמוּ וְנַעֲלֶ֣ה (oshb:Jer.6.4, byte tier) and ק֚וּמוּ וְנַעֲלֶ֣ה בַלָּ֔יְלָה וְנַשְׁחִ֖יתָה (oshb:Jer.6.5, byte tier), which both witnesses render in the first person plural as the attackers' own speech; the ruled granularity licenses this cut on a frame-owner CHANGE, and the change is asserted without the party being changed from ever being named. NEW FINDING, raised by neither item: the ground given for rejecting the strongest rival is byte-inexact at the exact verse the rival would cut. The rival is answered by saying the closing imperative is addressed to the same city already under address, but at MT 6:6 the city is governed by a preposition and is then spoken OF in the third person at הִ֚יא הָעִ֣יר הָפְקַ֔ד (oshb:Jer.6.6, byte tier), the verse closing on בְּקִרְבָּֽהּ (oshb:Jer.6.6, byte tier), and MT 6:7 continues third-person of her, whereas MT 6:8 names her as the vocative of a directly addressed imperative, הִוָּסְרִי֙ יְר֣וּשָׁלִַ֔ם (oshb:Jer.6.8, byte tier), with second-person suffixes at מִמֵּ֑ךְ and אֲשִׂימֵ֣ךְ (oshb:Jer.6.8, byte tier) that both witnesses render as address to the city. The addressee therefore CHANGES at MT 6:8, which is the ruled tier-1 explicit-addressee-shift class - the rival's live ground, and the one the row never answers. Verified sound and not disturbed: the setumah at MT 6:5 on the front seam and the petuchah at MT 6:8 on the row's own close are both correctly typed, kept apart, and held tier-3 single-witness non-driving; the inventory records exactly 1 variant note at MT 6:7 and the bytes bear it out, the unpointed reading standing immediately before the pointed one, disclosed without being quoted; and span-relevant disclosure symmetry is complete - the chapter's paseq segs stand at MT 6:1, 6:11, 6:14 and 6:16 (inventory: 4 segs in the chapter, 0 in span), and the inventories carry 0 special letters and 0 exegesis notes anywhere in MT 6:6-6:8. The seam stands; nothing here moves it.
rulings.remedy: Three field edits, no respan. (1) boundary_rationale - bring quote and gloss to one extent at MT 6:6: extend the Hebrew splice through the mound clause so it covers the English already offered, and add the receiving text's own rendering of the formula as its own balanced curly run in the same field, “For Yahweh of Armies said,” (web:Jer.6.6). CURE TEST (the test that killed the original): run the Hebrew word-run against the English word-run at MT 6:6 - every spliced word must have English beside it and every English word Hebrew behind it, with 0 words unmatched at either end; the extended splice must still return byte tier on re-collation; each curly run must be balanced and verbatim against the staged folded receiving text with a web: ref in the same field. (2) boundary_rationale - name the outgoing frame owner: state that Jer.6.4-Jer.6.5 is the attacking force's own first-person-plural summons, so the onset at Jer.6.6 is a frame-owner change and not a formula recurrence, and add web:Jer.6.4 to boundary_evidence_refs beside the web:Jer.6.5 already carried. CURE TEST: the outgoing mouth is named, not implied, and every verse argued in prose outside Jer.6.6-Jer.6.8 appears in boundary_evidence_refs. (3) strongest_rejected_alternative - replace the ground: the present sentence asserts the closing imperative addresses the same city already under address, which the bytes contradict (third-person reference to the city at Jer.6.6-Jer.6.7 against direct vocative address at Jer.6.8). Re-ground on what survives the shift - the mouth is unchanged, no fresh speech formula intervenes, and the Masoretic paragraph layer brackets Jer.6.6-Jer.6.8 as one segment (tier-3, single-witness, non-driving). CURE TEST: the sentence no longer asserts continuous address to the city, the ground given survives an explicit addressee shift at Jer.6.8, and the field stays within one sentence plus at most the mandated rival-disclosure second sentence. Then re-check confidence, presently high: if the rival is answered only by the unchanged mouth plus tier-3 paragraph corroboration, high is not carried and medium is the supported posture. NOT ordered and NOT author work: cutting Jer.6.8 into its own row is a boundary change and would need explicit adoption before anyone acts on it.
